question: Can enabled native motors with zero target velocity during zero-amplitude holding complete the unchanged recovery, four-cycle walking and 120-command settled-stop task?

selected_native_policy.activation: Valid V54 output with command.gait_amplitude exactly zero, including the first walking-session command. No role, seed, engine, command-number or observed-result selection.
selected_native_policy.law: After unchanged reference generation and validation, set each motor target velocity to zero. Preserve an already-zero value including signed zero. Motors stay enabled through the existing application path with unchanged impulse caps. Preserve requested/clamped position labels, all geometric references, phase progression and controller memory. Record the removed velocity and its delta in an additive native receipt and safety contribution.

tradeoffs.choice: Select enabled motors with zero velocity targets at zero gait amplitude
tradeoffs.benefit: Tests holding without the persistent position/rate feedback velocity requests observed under static references. Native motor reactions remain available within the existing caps; there is no new fitted numeric gain.
tradeoffs.risk: Joint position error can accumulate and contact or body motion can persist. Startup changes in both roles; copied-input agreement cannot predict physical settling.

tradeoffs.choice: Reduce the V53 velocity cap further
tradeoffs.decision: Not selected. The observed cap failed and the retained result does not identify a better nonzero cap.

tradeoffs.choice: Retune position gain or measured-rate damping
tradeoffs.decision: Deferred. These change the feedback dynamics and need a separately selected hypothesis; native motor braking tests a simpler holding behavior.

tradeoffs.choice: Move stop body/foot references or add measured support redistribution
tradeoffs.decision: Deferred as a distinct successor if braking fails. These alter desired geometry and require their own feasibility, slew and contact evidence.

tradeoffs.choice: Lengthen the stop or relax acceptance
tradeoffs.decision: Not selected. Keep the original 120-command stop, final 30 samples and every contact/motion requirement.

development_population.adequacy: Phase 241 covers the newly observed complete positive baseline and partial-recovery stopping failure. Phase 243 is a separate required prone diagnostic after a positive pair. Both are exposed development phases; neither is held-out evidence.

required_validation: Independently reconstruct all 1920 original R10M stop target readbacks, impulse observations and foot-load bindings; reject corrupted source, readback, identity and clock records.
Build a distinct V54 DLL with the complete native suite; preserve original V53/V52/V51 responses and earlier recovery fixtures byte-for-byte.

Exercise stateless and fresh-session APIs over both complete original R10M walking inputs, including the initial zero-amplitude command and all 120 stop commands. Verify exact zero targets, enabled-motor application semantics, unchanged nonzero-amplitude outputs, reference/memory identity, finite limits and no-actuation refusals.

Integrate a distinct R10N route through the actual Godot adapter, worker, report reader, finite evaluator and launcher. Run the complete applicable safety gate and negative controls before any physical child.
From a clean pushed freeze, run the fresh declared pair. Only an independently audited positive pair enables the fresh phase-243 prone diagnostic.
After successful development, declare and qualify a new held-out finite decision, retain its one-shot population and independently close and adopt successful evidence into QSDK-R10/M07.
